one_sentence_story: The moment you save a note or snap a quick photo, your brain stops memorizing the detail itself and stores only where to look it up.
so_what_for_you: Not knowing phone numbers by heart is smart brain bookkeeping, not memory decline. When a real-life moment truly matters, look with your own eyes for five full seconds before taking a photo.

jargon_map.plain: Handing a mental chore over to paper, folders, or cameras to save brain effort.
jargon_map.analogy: Setting heavy grocery bags on the counter so your hands are free to cook.

jargon_map.plain: Remembering who or what holds a fact instead of memorizing every word yourself.
jargon_map.analogy: Knowing your spouse keeps the tax receipts in the top desk drawer.

jargon_map.plain: Remembering less of a scene because clicking the camera cut your attention short.
jargon_map.analogy: Photocopying a page without ever reading a single line.
